EV_FINANCE.threshold_method: Maximum F1 on training cross-fitted OOF calibrated scores; illustrative marketing operating point, not financial eligibility.
EV_FINANCE.calibration_method: Regularised sigmoid (C=1) on training OOF logits; no validation/test fitting.
EV_FINANCE.confidence_method: Heuristic: (0.4 fold-model agreement + 0.3 key-input completeness + 0.3 training p1-p99 support) * min(1, training positives/100); not a probability of correctness.
EV_FINANCE.training_oof_note: Diagnostic only: CV model choice and cross-fitted calibration use training labels; validation/test are the independent estimates.

txn_categorisation.limitation: Customer-disjoint synthetic data shares merchant templates across splits; near-perfect scores do not establish generalisation to unseen banks or merchants.

methodology.data: Synthetic: 5000 customers, 684202 transactions; no real banking data
methodology.selection: Train-only 5-fold CV logloss: regularised logistic regression C grid vs LightGBM grid
methodology.validation: Independent validation: never used for model selection, calibration or threshold fitting
methodology.test: Same supplied customer split; original results inspected during audit. Fresh external/temporal test needed before real-world accuracy claims.
limitations: Synthetic take-up comes from a logistic label generator; linear models have a structural advantage
OOF training diagnostics can be optimistic after CV hyperparameter selection
Confidence is an input-quality/model-stability heuristic, not calibrated probability of correctness
Products passed by rules are candidates only; credit eligibility not assessed
